questions.question: Discuss the role of partition tolerance in a distributed system.
questions.solution_html:
• ANSWER: Partition tolerance ensures that if a group of nodes is unable to communicate
  • with other nodes due to network failures, the distributed system continues to operate
  • correctly.
  • Simplified Control and Management: Centralized systems offer easier governance
  • as there is a single authority making decisions and enforcing rules.
  • Single Point of Failure: If the central server fails, the whole system might be
  • compromised or rendered inoperable.
  • No Single Point of Failure: Multiple nodes provide redundancy and fault tolerance
  • enhancing reliability.
  • Complex Coordination: Achieving consensus across distributed nodes can be
  • resource-intensive and slow.
  • No Central Authority
  • o Bitcoin operates on a peer-to-peer network where no single entity
  • government, or organization controls the issuance, validation, or
  • management of the currency.
  • o Transactions are verified by miners and recorded on a distributed public
  • ledger (blockchain).
  • Entity authentication
  • Entity authentication is the assurance that an entity is currently involved and active in a
  • communication session.

questions.question: Discuss the role of consensus algorithms in blockchain.
questions.solution_html:
• ANSWER: Consensus is a distributed computing concept that has been used in
  • blockchain in order to provide a means of agreeing to a single version of the truth by all
  • peers on the blockchain network.

  • single point of control.
  • Disadvantages

  • lead to trust issues.

  • lack of central control.

  • independently validate and store copies of all transactions.
  • o This ensures immutability and resilience against tampering or central
  • control.

questions.question: Explain the concept of decentralization in blockchain technology.
questions.solution_html:
• ANSWER: This is a core concept and benefit of the blockchain. There is no need for a
  • trusted third party or intermediary to validate transactions; instead, a consensus
  • mechanism is used to agree on the validity of transactions.
  • Consensus Mechanism – Proof of Work (PoW)
  • o Bitcoin uses a PoW consensus mechanism, requiring miners to solve
  • complex computational puzzles to add blocks to the chain.
  • o This secures the network without needing a trusted third party.
questions.final_answer: o This secures the network without needing a trusted third party

questions.question: Define and examine asymmetric cryptography.
questions.solution_html:
• ANSWER: Asymmetric cryptography refers to a type of cryptography where the key that
  • is used to encrypt the data is different from the key that is used to decrypt the data. This
  • is also known as public key cryptography. It uses both public and private keys to encrypt
  • and decrypt data, respectively. Various asymmetric cryptography schemes are in use
  • including RSA, DSA, and ElGammal.
  • Limited Supply
  • o Bitcoin has a fixed supply cap of 21 million coins, and its issuance is
  • governed by an algorithm—not human policy—ensuring predictability and
  • scarcity.

questions.question: Explain the role of decentralization in blockchain technology and how it / transforms traditional system.
questions.solution_html:
• transforms traditional system.
  • ANSWER: Decentralization is a fundamental principle of blockchain technology that
  • significantly transforms traditional systems. In conventional centralized models, a single
  • authority or intermediary controls data and operations, making systems vulnerable to
  • failure, manipulation, and inefficiencies. Blockchain replaces this centralized structure
  • with a decentralized network where control is distributed among multiple independent
  • nodes. These nodes participate in decision-making through consensus mechanisms like
  • Proof of Work (PoW), eliminating the need for trusted third parties. This shift enhances
  • transparency, security, and fault tolerance by ensuring that no single point of failure can
  • disrupt the system. Moreover, decentralization empowers users by giving them direct
  • control over their data and transactions. It enables the development of new applications
  • and paradigms where services can operate autonomously, transparently, and without
  • centralized oversight. As a result, blockchain decentralization redefines how information
  • systems are structured, promoting fairness, resilience, and trust across various sectors
  • (also include methods of decentralization).

questions.final_answer: Why Bitcoin Is Considered a Decentralized Currency

questions.question: Analyse Confidentiality, Integrity, and Authentication in cryptographic / systems.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse Confidentiality, Integrity, and Authentication in cryptographic systems.
  • ANSWER: Cryptography is the science of making information secure in the presence of
  • adversaries. It does so under the assumption that limitless resources are available to
  • adversaries. Ciphers are algorithms used to encrypt or decrypt data, so that if intercepted
  • by an adversary, the data is meaningless to them without decryption, which requires a
  • secret key. Cryptography is primarily used to provide a confidentiality service.
  • In addition to a confidentiality service, cryptography also provides other security services
  • such as integrity, authentication (entity authentication and data origin authentication)
  • and non-repudiation. Additionally, accountability is also provided, which is a requirement
  • in many security systems.
  • Confidentiality
  • Confidentiality is the assurance that information is only available to authorized entities.
  • Integrity
  • Integrity is the assurance that information is modifiable only by authorized entities.
  • Authentication
  • Authentication provides assurance about the identity of an entity or the validity of a
  • message. There are two types of authentication mechanisms, namely entity
  • authentication and data origin authentication.

questions.question: Differentiate the different layers of a decentralized ecosystem and / explain their functions.
questions.solution_html:
• functions.
  • ANSWER: To achieve complete decentralization, it is necessary that the environment
  • around the blockchain also be decentralized. The blockchain is a distributed ledger that
  • runs on top of conventional systems. These elements include storage, communication
  • and computation. There are other factors, such as identity and wealth, which are
  • traditionally based on centralized paradigms, and there's a need to decentralize these
  • aspects as well in order to achieve a sufficiently decentralized ecosystem.
  • Storage
  • Data can be stored directly in a blockchain, and with this fact it achieves
  • decentralization. However, a significant disadvantage of this approach is that a
  • blockchain is not suitable for storing large amounts of data by design. It can store
  • simple transactions and some arbitrary data, but it is certainly not suitable for
  • storing images or large blobs of data, as is the case with traditional database
  • systems. A better alternative for storing data is to use Distributed Hash Tables
  • (DHTs). DHTs were used initially in peer-to-peer file sharing software, such as
  • BitTorrent, Napster, Kazaa, and Gnutella.
  • Two primary requirements here are high availability and link stability, which means
  • that data should be available when required and network links also should always
  • be accessible.
  • The incentive mechanism for storing data is based on a protocol known as
  • Filecoin, which pays incentives to nodes that store data using the Bitswap
  • mechanism.
  • Communication
  • The internet (the communication layer in blockchain) is considered to be
  • decentralized.
  • This model is based on unconditional trust of a central authority (the service
  • provider) where users are not in control of their data. Even user passwords are
  • stored on trusted third-party systems. Thus, there is a need to provide control to
  • individual users in such a way that access to their data is guaranteed and is not
  • dependent on a single third party. Access to the internet (the communication
  • layer) is based on Internet Service Providers (ISPs) who act as a central hub for
  • internet users.
  • An alternative is to use mesh networks. Even though they are limited in
  • functionality when compared to the internet, they still provide a decentralized
  • alternative where nodes can talk directly to each other without a central hub such
  • as an ISP.
  • Computing power and decentralization
  • Decentralization of computing or processing power is achieved by a blockchain
  • technology such as Ethereum, where smart contracts with embedded business
  • logic can run on the blockchain network. Other blockchain technologies also
  • provide similar processing-layer platforms, where business logic can run over the
  • network in a decentralized manner.

questions.question: Recommend a secure setup process for installing and using a Bitcoin / wallet.
questions.solution_html:
• Recommend a secure setup process for installing and using a Bitcoin wallet.
  • ANSWER: 1. Choose the Right Wallet Type (Define wallets and its types in detail)
  • ● Hardware Wallets (e.g., Ledger, Trezor): Best for long-term storage; they store
  • keys offline, making them resistant to malware.
  • ● Software Wallets
  • o Desktop Wallets: Offer better security than mobile/web wallets but are
  • more vulnerable than hardware wallets.
  • o Mobile Wallets: Convenient but less secure; best for small amounts.
  • o Web Wallets: Most convenient but least secure; avoid for large holdings.
  • ● Paper Wallets: Involve printing your keys and storing them physically; high risk if
  • not handled correctly.

  • ANSWER: 1. Choose the Right Wallet Type (Define wallets and its types in detail)
  • ● Hardware Wallets (e.g., Ledger, Trezor): Best for long-term storage; they store
  • keys offline, making them resistant to malware.
  • ● Software Wallets
  • o Desktop Wallets: Offer better security than mobile/web wallets but are
  • more vulnerable than hardware wallets.
  • o Mobile Wallets: Convenient but less secure; best for small amounts.
  • o Web Wallets: Most convenient but least secure; avoid for large holdings.
  • ● Paper Wallets: Involve printing your keys and storing them physically; high risk if
  • not handled correctly.
